Subject: TTFT + streaming cadence follow-up from today's call

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the call earlier - good to meet you and the Acme AI team. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on performance/SLO requirements before an engineering sync:

- TTFT target: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 400 ms (you flagged p95 as the primary objective)
- Streaming: prefer WebSocket for bidirectional interactions, but SSE is acceptable for uni-directional flows
- Chunk cadence: target chunks every ~150-250 ms under steady-state; can also support token-based chunking (e.g., 256-512 token windows) if that maps better to your client
- Concurrency/throughput: you mentioned ~50 concurrent active users with peaks up to ~1,000 requests/minute (we'll validate sizing on the tech call)

Attached our streaming playbook (redwood_streaming_playbook.pdf) and a short questionnaire to capture sample payloads. Can you confirm the following so we can size a test environment?
- Typical prompt length (avg tokens) and worst-case tokens
- Expected percentage of streaming requests vs non-streaming requests
- Preferred protocol (WebSocket vs SSE) and TLS termination preferences

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-minute tech sync with Vivek + Rishi to validate runtime config and test harness (I'm flexible tomorrow 10-11am PT or Monday 9-11am PT)
2) You share a short sample prompt and expected token distribution (attach as a doc if easier)
3) We'll produce a draft SLO proposal + rough cost/infra estimate and baseline TTFT test plan

Attachment: redwood_streaming_playbook.pdf (application/pdf, 180KB)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hey Marissa -

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifications from our side:

- TTFT: p95 <= 250 ms sounds right as our target. For budgeting we'll want to understand p99 impact but aren't setting hard p99 goals yet (we saw p99 spikes up to ~600 ms in our current infra during peak).
- Concurrency/Throughput: 50 active concurrent users is accurate for our initial pilot; peak throughput is closer to 800-1,200 requests/minute depending on user activity - often spiky around product launches.
- Streaming: WebSocket is our preference since we sometimes need client acknowledgements and backpressure signaling.
- Chunk cadence: 200 ms cadence is acceptable; we generally aim for ~200 ms per chunk to keep UI snappy.

I've attached a short doc with our estimated token histograms and a sample interactive payload (acme_ttft_requirements.pdf).

We can do the tech sync tomorrow at 10:30am PT if that works for Vivek and Rishi.

Subject: Re: TTFT + streaming cadence requirements — technical notes

Alex / Marissa -

Thanks for the context. A few early technical notes ahead of tomorrow's sync:

- TTFT under 250 ms (p95) is achievable with the right config. Key levers:
  - Use low-latency runtime mode (disable large batching windows; set max_batch_delay to <= 2 ms for interactive paths)
  - Warmed KV-cache and pinned model shards to avoid cold-starts
  - Prefer smaller tokenization chunk sizes on client side (we can recommend 128-256 token buffer increments if UI allows)

- Streaming protocol: WebSocket is fine and gives better control for acks/backpressure. We'll recommend a lightweight keepalive and a path to fall back to SSE if client restrictions exist.

- Chunk cadence: 150-200 ms is a good target. If your client prefers token-count triggers, we can match 256-token or 512-token boundaries - for TTFT, time-based cadence is usually more important than token count.

- Test harness: we'll need sample payloads, average and 95th token lengths, and a target concurrency profile. If you can share a simple CSV with timestamped request sizes, we can run a pre-prod baseline.

I'll join tomorrow at 10:30am PT and will bring a short checklist of runtime flags and a draft load test plan.

Vivek Kulkarni
